title: Sunny
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Children at the Star Kids home, a group home for abandoned and orphaned children, cope with ordinary growing pains and the particular ache of having been left. Their refuge is an old Nissan Sunny car on the lawn, where in imagination they can travel anywhere. Taiyō Matsumoto drew partly on his own childhood.
life_message: Children who have been let down still deserve wonder, belonging and someone who stays.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Home rules balanced by the free space of the Sunny car.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Children long for absent parents; the home becomes substitute kin.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Older kids and caregivers guide younger ones.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Rural 1970s Japan, little religion shown (to verify).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Imaginative play and self-expression amid hardship.

folkways.japan: The stigma of being placed in a group home reflects Japanese emphasis on family registry and belonging, described in the story through the children's shame.

delivery.note: Its outlook on abandoned children is carried by everyday episodes at the group home rather than stated lessons.

winners_losers: The children's resilience gets full sympathy; absent parents are mourned more than blamed.
